new.analysis:
The green light here is the shin: pain 0/10 on all three runs, quiet the next morning, and heart rate sitting calmly in zones 1 and 2. That is exactly the signal that permits a small next step rather than a repeat.

The step I am taking is on the running intervals, not the number of days or the pace. You go from roughly 1 minute of running at a time to 1 minute 30, keeping the walk breaks equal so the shin has recovery inside the session. Weekly running time rises from about 15 to about 22 minutes, and the longest session nudges from 15 to 18 minutes, which is within the 2 to 3 minute per step guideline.

Everything stays easy on purpose. No strides, no hills, no pushing the pace even when it feels silly slow; the shin loads the same whether you jog or trot, and the point right now is adding minutes without adding stress. Keep the physio calf and hip work on your off days, since that is doing quiet work in the background.

The rule for the week is simple: if the shin aches above a 3/10 during a run, stop and walk home, and if it is louder the next morning, we repeat this week instead of adding next week. Tell me how each run felt and we will keep stepping forward from there.

safetyCallouts.title: Shin check-in rule.
safetyCallouts.body: If the shin aches above 3/10 during a run, or feels worse the next morning, stop the session and message your physio before the next run. We will repeat rather than progress until it is quiet again.
